descriptionText: Self-hosted runners in public repositories pose significant security risks due to potential persistence between workflow runs. Unlike GitHub-hosted runners which are ephemeral and cleaned between each job, self-hosted runners may retain state, files, and credentials from previous executions. In public repositories, this is especially dangerous as any user can open a pull request that triggers workflows on these runners, potentially accessing secrets, modifying the runner environment, or establishing persistence for future attacks. Self-hosted runners are identified by the 'self-hosted' label as the first element in the runs-on configuration. Expression-based runner selection is also flagged as it may expand to self-hosted runners at runtime.
